title: The Tale of the Heike (Heike monogatari)

access.edition_or_version: Helen Craig McCullough translation, Stanford University Press, 1988 (consulted as locator)

tone_mechanisms_observed: opening meditation on the impermanence of all things (mujo)
the fall of the proud as emblem of transience
recurring seasonal and natural imagery of decline
collective elegy for a defeated clan
mechanics.emotional_progression: Grand opening on impermanence -> rise and fall of a warrior house -> lament for the fallen.
mechanics.point_of_view: Recited narrative voice, moving between court and battlefield.
mechanics.rhythm_and_cadence: Prose with embedded verse; rhetorical repetition suited to oral recitation.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Public, communal mourning rather than private confession; distance is doctrinal (Buddhist impermanence).
mechanics.style_and_devices: The canonical Japanese exemplar of mono no aware / mujo, cited by Parkes SEP. Described, not quoted.
mechanics.copyright_note: Source text public domain; the 1988 translation is copyrighted. Described by technique only; no passage reproduced.
